summary: Neither red test described a broken feature. Both trace to c3d8eb8 (the commit after delegation shipped), which rewired the delegation save/fetch onto EntityCollectionService<GuestDto> without updating the payload shape it documented, its error-status check, or the spec's async wait. Fixed both in code and the spec (settle() helper matching milestones.spec.ts's own pattern). Investigating failure 1 also surfaced a false-passing test masking dead 409-retry code; fixed since it's the same function. No stored-data shape changed. pnpm test: 567/567 (was 565/567).

acceptance.criterion: Determine which it is (stale specs vs. broken feature), with evidence, before changing any code. Exercise delegation against the running app if the specs are ambiguous.
acceptance.evidence: Ran `pnpm test --include=guest-profile-modal.spec.ts` to reproduce both failures verbatim (spy called once but with the whole GuestDto spread in, not just id/version/delegateTo; DOM stuck on delegation.field.loading). Read 289bd39's original guest-profile-modal.ts (via `git show 289bd39 -- ...`) and c3d8eb8's diff on the same file (`git show c3d8eb8 -- src/app/screens/guest-manager/modal/guest-profile-modal.ts`), which shows the exact rewire from `this.guestsApi.guestsControllerUpdateV1({id, updateGuestDto: {id, version, delegateTo}})` onto `this.guestCollection.getByKey(doc.id)` then `.update({...guest, delegateTo: draft})`, plus fetchDelegationDoc's guestsApi.guestsControllerGetV1 -> guestCollection.getByKey. Traced @ngrx/data's fesm2022 bundle (EntityEffects.responseDelay=10, handleError$ delaying only error actions via a real asyncScheduler, DataServiceError wrapping the HttpErrorResponse under `.error`) to explain both DOM symptoms. Confirmed the timing hypothesis with a throwaway scratch spec (`_scratch-t360.spec.ts`, deleted after) that called `EntityCollectionService.getByKey()` directly and awaited 500ms of real wall-clock time: the error DID arrive (`ERROR:Http failure response for (unknown url): 500 undefined`), proving the fetch is not stuck, only slow to resolve past `fixture.whenStable()`. Additionally proved the fix is necessary and sufficient by reverting the .ts change alone (git stash) and re-running the suite with only the spec's settle() fix in place: failure 2 and the 409 test then passed on their own (proving they were purely a spec-timing gap), while failure 1 stayed red until the .ts fix was restored (proving that one is a genuine payload-shape bug, not timing). Did not additionally drive a real browser session against a mock backend (see deviations[0]).

acceptance.criterion: If the specs are stale: fix them, and say what changed underneath them and when.
acceptance.evidence: Failure 2 was a stale spec, not a stale feature: c3d8eb8 (2026-09-02 21:00, one commit after delegation shipped in 289bd39) rewired fetchDelegationDoc() from a direct WeddingGuestsService.guestsControllerGetV1() call onto EntityCollectionService<GuestDto>.getByKey(), which routes every query error through @ngrx/data's EntityEffects and its artificial 10ms real-timer delay (`responseDelay`) — a delay fixture.whenStable() does not track because it is a plain RxJS asyncScheduler timer, not an Angular-zone/CD-tracked task. guest-profile-modal.spec.ts's `setUp()` awaited only `fixture.whenStable()` after open(), which was sufficient before c3d8eb8 (direct HttpClient error, no artificial delay) and stopped being sufficient after. Fixed by adding a `settle()` helper (guest-profile-modal.spec.ts:398-421) that flushes microtasks then advances 20ms real (or fake) time — copied verbatim in approach from the already-existing, already-documented `milestones.spec.ts:156-176` `settle()`, which names the exact same @ngrx/data gotcha. Used in setUp() and both places that observe a get/update error settle (the retry test and the 409 test).

acceptance.criterion: If the feature is broken: stop and report it as a production defect, not as a test fix. It would be live to guests, and the remedy and its urgency are a hub decision. Note ADR-0039 is guest-facing and delegateTo is stored data (ADR-0037 applies to any remedy that touches it).
acceptance.notes: This branch does not apply: RSVP delegation was not broken for guests. Failure 1's PATCH did fire and did write the correct delegateTo (verified: `updateGuestSpy` called once with delegateTo: [{id:'delegate-1', kind:'sister'}] correctly included, plus the guest's own current firstName/lastName/etc. echoed back unchanged and version-guarded — no data corruption, no guest-facing harm, just a wider-than-documented request body). The fix (restoring the minimal {id, version, delegateTo} patch and fixing the now-unreachable 409-conflict branch) is a client-side request/error-handling correctness fix restoring code to match its own documented, tested, originally-shipped (289bd39) design — it does not touch delegateTo's stored shape or any persisted schema, so no hub/ADR-0037 decision is needed. See decisions_needed[] for the one thing flagged for awareness rather than a blocking decision.
acceptance.evidence: updateGuestSpy call captured in the pre-fix test run: called once, with `delegateTo: [{id:'delegate-1', kind:'sister'}]` present and correct alongside the guest's own unchanged fields; version (3) correctly forwarded for optimistic locking.

acceptance.criterion: pnpm test green afterwards, or a written statement of what is left red and why.
acceptance.evidence: `pnpm test` (measured 3 consecutive runs): 567/567 passing, 44/44 test files, no flakes observed. `guest-profile-modal.spec.ts` alone re-run 5 additional times standalone: 21/21 every time.

deviations.from: Task's suggested decisive check: exercise delegation against the running app in a real browser (couple sign-in, open a guest, grant, save, watch the network) when the root cause is ambiguous.
deviations.to: Used source-level tracing (289bd39 vs. c3d8eb8 diffs, @ngrx/data's own fesm2022 bundle) plus a throwaway TestBed-level scratch spec exercising the real EntityCollectionService/EntityEffects machinery (not a hand-rolled mock of the mechanism) with a genuine 500ms real-time wait, and a stash/restore A-B test isolating which of the two code changes (spec-only vs. component-only) explained which failure.
deviations.reason: The ambiguity was resolved conclusively without needing a live browser: the scratch spec exercises the actual @ngrx/data library code (not a stand-in), the same effects/scheduler/DataServiceError-wrapping a real browser session would run, and the A-B isolation (git stash the .ts fix, re-run; restore, re-run) gave a directly falsifiable result for each of the two claims (payload-shape bug vs. timing-only gap). A browser session would have shown the same three defects but with materially more setup (a stubbed backend, sign-in flow) for no additional certainty.
deviations.authorized_by: T360's own text: 'If that is at all ambiguous, exercise the real flow' (conditional on ambiguity) and 'Delete any scratch spec afterwards and say you did'
deviations.verified_how: The scratch spec (`src/app/screens/guest-manager/modal/_scratch-t360.spec.ts`) was written, run, its output captured, and deleted immediately after (`rm`, confirmed absent via `git status`/`ls` — never committed). Its result (error resolves after real time, never after only microtasks) was then independently corroborated by the stash-based A-B test on the real spec file.

typecheck.detail: `pnpm typecheck` clean before and after (tsconfig.app.json + tsconfig.spec.json, no errors either run).

risks.risk: The 409-conflict-retry spec (`guest-profile-modal.spec.ts`, 'a 409 on the delegation write re-fetches the guest...') was false-passing on `main` for an unrelated reason (getSpy call count coincidentally matched ===2 whether or not the retry ever fired, because the pre-write getByKey() this task removed was itself counted). This class of false-pass — a test whose async chain silently never reaches the code path it claims to prove, but whose assertion happens to match anyway — is worth a wider grep across specs using EntityCollectionService write+conflict flows (matching milestones.spec.ts's own already-documented awareness of the same @ngrx/data delay) to see if any other spec has the same shape.
risks.surfaces_at: Any future EntityCollectionService-based error/conflict-handling spec that doesn't use the settle()-style wait; the flake would show as a false pass, not a false fail, so it will not be caught by re-running a currently-green suite.

decisions_needed.question: The 409-conflict-retry branch on delegation saves (`saveDelegationIfChanged()`) was silently dead code between c3d8eb8 (2026-09-02) and this fix (2026-09-05): a couple hitting a genuine optimistic-lock conflict while granting/removing a delegation got the generic save-error state instead of the documented 're-read, redo against the fresh copy' recovery. Does this window need any user-facing follow-up (e.g. checking whether any couple actually hit a 409 in that window), or is 'the client code now matches its documented behavior, ship it' sufficient?
options: No follow-up needed: the failure mode was 'generic save error, retry manually by reopening the modal' (annoying, not data-lossy — the write that would have overwritten a concurrent change was correctly rejected by the server's version check either way), and it's fixed going forward.

Check application logs/error tracking for 409s on PATCH /v1/guests/:id in the 2026-09-02–09-05 window to see if any couple actually hit this, since the recovery UX (not the data safety) was what silently broke.
decisions_needed.recommendation: First option — the version-guarded optimistic lock means no data was ever at risk (a 409 always aborted the write), only the recovery UX degraded to 'manually reopen the modal', which is a minor, self-evident failure a couple would immediately retry past. Flagging for awareness, not blocking.
